note: The layers the viewer can draw: each maps a record a run saved, or a number worked out from saved ones by a declared rule, to a mark. A record is named as a run's view names it: the engine's own readout name, or the name an adapter gave it, in the order tried. Where a layer lists several quantities (first_of), it takes the first the run can feed: the engine's own readout where the run kept it, a worked-out number otherwise. A rule with several inputs names, for each part it is worked out from, what may fill it, in the order tried: a record the run saved, a named constant of its definition (stated by the run's view only where nothing the run schedules changes it), or an amount over a volume. A layer is offered for a run only when the run saved what it needs; what a run did not save is said. A record laid over the cells that no layer here names is still offered as a colouring and a relief, under the record's own name. Ion traffic (idea 5) is declared and its mark has its place; it draws once a run saved the amounts transferred. The layers of ideas 6 and 7 are added as their marks are built.

layers.label: Membrane voltage
layers.says: Each cell is coloured by its membrane voltage.

layers.label: Membrane voltage
layers.says: Each cell stands as high as its membrane voltage. Nothing is smoothed between cells.

layers.label: Voltage drops

also.says: A hollow wedge: the junction's gate is under half open.
also.without: This run did not save each junction's gate, so every wedge is drawn solid.

also.says: Two bars: the two cells differ in voltage, and no junction has formed between them.
also.without: This run did not save how far each junction has formed, so a wedge is drawn wherever the voltages differ.

layers.says: A wedge on a junction points down the voltage drop across it, and is as wide as the drop is large. It is a difference of voltages, not a current: it never moves.

layers.label: Push and pull on ions
layers.says: For each ion at the chosen cell's membrane: the push of its concentration difference, the pull of the voltage, and what is left of the two, in millivolts. An arrow is a drive, not a flow: it never moves.

layers.label: Membrane charge
layers.says: Plus and minus marks at the two faces of the chosen cell's membrane, as many as the charge its voltage stands for on a piece of that size. How many there are is worked out; where each sits is illustration.

layers.label: Ion traffic

also.says: Beads through a pump: its cycles between two records, each cycle moving the ions the run's definition gives it.
also.without: This run did not save its pumps' cycles, so no beads cross through a pump.

also.says: Beads through the membrane itself: what crossed it beside its channels.
also.without: This run did not save what crossed the membrane beside its channels.

layers.says: Beads cross the chosen cell's membrane through each of its channel populations and pumps, as many a second as the run's saved totals grew between two records. A bead is a token of a rate, not an ion: the legend says how many ions one stands for and what time the picture keeps.
